Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

The best pitching matchup of the day, wrapped in a division-clinching afterglow — this one's worth your evening. Fresh off popping champagne for their fourth straight NL Central title, the Brewers roll into PNC Park with baseball's top gNERD score today (17.74), and the arms are the reason why. Rookie Logan Henderson (10-3, 2.34 ERA) starts as he tries to push the Brewers toward the NL's top seed, opposing Jared Jones in a rematch of their August 4 meeting in Milwaukee, which the Brewers won 4-2. Henderson's a legitimately fun watch: he has issued only 15 free passes all season, and he has never allowed more than three runs in any of his 20 career starts. Jones, whose 9.87 pNERD tops the day thanks to elite velocity and whiff rates, has been quietly dazzling himself — he hasn't allowed a run in his past two starts, a stretch of 13 innings. Milwaukee's lineup backs it up, ranking near the top of the league in batting and baserunning value, with a young, cost-efficient roster that overperforms its payroll. Pittsburgh's offense is thin, but strong bullpen and baserunning marks keep them respectable. Two power arms, a playoff-seeding subplot, and a division champ still hungry — good stuff.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Zack Wheeler's return from the surgical table is the whole show here, and it's worth watching even against a Nationals team playing out the string. Wheeler, who had a rib removed to fix thoracic outlet syndrome after his 2025 season ended early, has been working his way back from the medical condition and subsequent surgery that ended his 2025 season, in his first big-league starts since being shut down in August 2025. The numbers suggest he's found his stuff again — his 8.28 pNERD is well above the historic 95th percentile, driven by an excellent xFIP- and a swinging-strike rate that's climbed into elite territory, plus mid-90s velocity that shows the surgery hasn't sapped his arm strength. Across the mound, Jared Simpson brings a pNERD of zero, meaning there's simply no track record to grade — a blank slate rather than a red flag. The Nationals counter with real juice on offense: standout barrel rate, baserunning, and a young, cheap roster that all push their tNERD to 8.56, comfortably above average. The Phillies' shaky bullpen luck and lower payroll bump drag their team score down, but with a 13.29 gNERD, this game sits above both the historic and today's averages — worth a look mostly for Wheeler.

San Francisco Giants @ St. Louis Cardinals, 10:15a

Summary

A rebuilding-year matchup redeemed almost entirely by an interesting pitching curiosity, not by the surrounding baseball. Anthony Molina brings a 9.61 pNERD—well above today's 5.04 average—built on mid-90s-plus velocity, a favorable xFIP-, and youth (24), though his 6.63 ERA tells a very different story than the underlying metrics suggest; he's a August trade-deadline pickup traded to the San Francisco Giants in exchange for Tyler Mahle and recalled up to the team for the first time on August 24, and has made three big league starts since the trade and has never recorded more than 15 outs, so don't expect length. Across from him, Liberatore owns a respectable 6.29 pNERD but comes in with a rough year, sitting 5-14 with a 5.53 ERA and 1.49 WHIP, and a 1.486 WHIP means baserunners arrive constantly, with 3.3 walks per nine inflating pitch counts—expect both bullpens to get plenty of work. The gNERD of 12.75 sits comfortably above the historical median (10.80) thanks almost entirely to pitcher scores, since team quality is middling: the Cardinals' 5.89 tNERD gets a boost from a young, cheap roster, while the Giants' 3.72 mark reflects a club that didn't go the way anyone in the front office intended and will likely lose 95 or more games. Watch for velocity and swing-and-miss from Molina early, then settle in for a bullpen game.

Chicago White Sox @ Cleveland Guardians, 10:10a

Summary

A tight AL Central race with a real strikeout mismatch on the mound makes this one worth carving out time for. Cleveland sits half a game behind Chicago with the head-to-head tiebreaker now in play, so as one outlet put it, "every game between these two clubs now carries direct postseason weight, with no buffer left for either side." The pitching matchup tilts heavily toward Cleveland's Parker Messick, whose 8.10 pNERD is comfortably above average - he's coming off a 12-strikeout display against the Detroit Tigers on September 5 and has eclipsed his strikeout projection in 7 of his last 10 starts. His low xFIP- and quick pace make him genuinely fun to watch. Anthony Kay, by contrast, offers a modest fastball but little else, and reports have him cratered over his recent outings. Both lineups carry decent tNERD marks, with Chicago's bullpen and low payroll/age both adding value, and Cleveland's baserunning and radio charm doing the same, despite a weak barrel rate. Overall, at 12.67 gNERD this sits comfortably above today's average - one worth watching mainly for Messick and the standings stakes.

Boston Red Sox @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

Boston's rookie lefty with a chess player's command squares off against Texas's strikeout artist who can't stop the bleeding — a pitching matchup that's more interesting than the standings gap suggests. Jake Bennett, a 25-year-old rookie making his MLB debut season, brings excellent control to the mound — he has walked just 19 batters in 105 innings, a rate of 1.6 per nine, with command as his edge — though he's coming off his worst outing of the year, having given up six earned runs and three home runs over 5.1 innings against the Angels. That earns him a strong 7.16 pNERD, boosted by youth and elite strike-throwing. Gore, meanwhile, has been scuffling: he has not completed six innings in five straight starts, and over his last four has thrown 16 innings, allowed 14 earned runs and issued 14 walks, though his stuff still ticks positive at 5.92 pNERD thanks to plus velocity and whiff rates. Both team NERDs are middling — Boston's bullpen and fielding pull weight, Texas leans on batting runs and a healthy dose of good luck. Boston enters at 82-69, third in the AL East and firmly in the Wild Card race, while Texas sits at 75-76, giving Boston postseason stakes Texas mostly lacks. At 12.65 gNERD, this sits comfortably above the historic average — worth a look, mainly for the pitching.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:40p

Summary

Blake Snell is pitching like a man with something to prove, and that alone makes this worth a look even if the Reds don't put up much of a fight. Snell has returned from elbow surgery on an absolute heater, and his pNERD of 9.64 backs it up — he's not allowed more than one run in any of his six starts back, riding a filthy swinging-strike rate and a sub-3.00 xFIP- that suggests the results are real, not mirage. Across town, Andrew Abbott is having the opposite kind of September: he's 6-11 with a 4.78 ERA, and his last outing ended after two innings against Milwaukee in a 20-0 blowout, which is reflected in his modest 2.27 pNERD. The Dodgers (8.09 tNERD) bring the superior lineup and bullpen, while Cincinnati's offense — batting .229 as a team over this series — gives Snell little to worry about. This gNERD of 12.33 sits a bit above the historical median and slightly above today's average, driven almost entirely by pitching mismatch rather than competitive tension; watch for Snell's stuff, not for suspense.

Atlanta Braves @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Playoff stakes and a lopsided pitching matchup make this Wrigley finale worth a look, even if the on-mound drama leans heavily one direction. Atlanta arrives in first place in the NL East, while Chicago is clinging to a wild-card spot, and the Braves and Cubs close out their series at Wrigley Field with Chicago's Wild Card hopes on the line, with a loss stinging that much more for the home club. The Cubs' offense has been the story of their season: their gaudy 10.08 tNERD is fueled by elite batting and fielding runs, and it's easy to see why given a surging core led by Pete Crow-Armstrong (42 HR), Alex Bregman and Seiya Suzuki. Atlanta counters with a more middling 5.30 tNERD, propped up by a solid bullpen but dragged by shaky baserunning, though Ronald Acuña Jr. and Matt Olson give the lineup teeth. On the mound, it's polish versus prospect: Imanaga, working on a strong 5.98 pNERD, has been about efficiency and command, with only 37 walks in 162.1 innings, while rookie JR Ritchie (2.38 pNERD) has been wild, with 53 strikeouts and 36 walks in just 58 innings. The 11.88 gNERD sits a shade above average, worth watching for the stakes and Imanaga's craft more than any pitching duel.

New York Yankees @ Minnesota Twins, 10:40a

Summary

The Yankees look poised to complete a sweep of a fading Twins team, and the numbers back up the mismatch as entertainment. New York enters having won the first two games of this series by a combined 16-4, riding a stretch where they're winners of seven of their last eight games. Carlos Rodón, back on track after an offseason elbow surgery scare, has allowed two earned runs or less in each of his last six starts since returning from the Injured List with an elbow issue — his pNERD of 4.00 undersells how sharp he's been lately, even if his strike-throwing z-score still lags. Across the mound, Zebby Matthews carries real swing-and-miss stuff (his velocity and youth push his pNERD to 6.04, tops in this game) but is in search of his first win in three September starts after a disaster outing where he allowed five earned runs in just 2.1 innings against Detroit. Minnesota's playoff hopes are on life support, and losing Buxton for the year doesn't help. The 10.32 gNERD sits almost exactly at the historical median — watchable mostly for Rodón's bounce-back and a possible laugher, not a marquee pitching duel.

Both teams are still fighting for something even if neither is thrilling: Arizona is 2.5 games back of a wild-card spot with the calendar running out, while Miami is playing spoiler after arriving on a modest winning streak despite sitting well outside the race. That late-September stakes gap gives this one a pulse even though the underlying NERD math says it's a middle-of-the-road watch.

Miami's tNERD (8.99) is the story on the offense side — a young, cheap roster that's been unlucky relative to its output, with strong baserunning value, though thin on barrels. Arizona's tNERD (5.69) leans on plus fielding and baserunning but a below-average bat, and its more expensive, older roster doesn't get the youth/payroll bonus Miami's does. On the mound, Ryan Gusto (pNERD 4.08) has been quietly effective, having allowed two earned runs or less in six of his last seven starts, and his exceptional strike-throwing is the best thing going for either pitcher tonight. Merrill Kelly (pNERD 1.66), at 37, is fighting an xFIP- north of 118 and diminished velocity, making him the weaker link. Overall gNERD of 10.21 sits almost exactly at the historical median and just below today's slate average — a solidly average game elevated slightly by playoff-race tension rather than pitching brilliance.

Padres at Coors Field, chasing a wild card spot, against a Rockies team playing out the string — that's the setup, and it's more interesting for San Diego's stakes than for anything happening on the mound. The Padres bring by far the better roster here, with strong fielding, baserunning, and a bullpen that's been one of the league's best, and it shows in a tNERD of 10.41 that's near the top of what you'll see even by today's standards. Colorado, buried at 56-95 and eliminated from contention, checks in near replacement level across the board, though rookie righty Mason Adams has quietly outpitched his record with a 3.38 ERA across 18.2 innings and gives Denver at least a puncher's chance. Add in Coors Field's altitude-fueled chaos and a season series the Padres have dominated 9-1, and this shapes up as an offense-forward laugher rather than a pitching duel — watchable for the stakes and the scoreboard, not the artistry.

Nick Martinez has quietly had an All-Star-caliber year — 14-4 with a 2.92 ERA and 1.07 WHIP over 166 1/3 innings — but his xFIP- of 108 suggests some regression is fair, and his 3.34 pNERD reflects a modest package built mostly on strike-throwing rather than bat-missing. Tampa Bay's offense is playing far better than expected (positive batting-runs, +0.98 z-score) while the barrel rate is oddly low for a good-hitting team — a quirky contrast worth noting. With a gNERD of 8.30, this sits below the historical average (10.81) and near the low end of today's slate (6.09–17.74), so treat it as background baseball rather than appointment viewing.

I've got enough to write the summary now.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's magic number to clinch the NL Central is two, and Jacob Misiorowski's turn to pitch happens to fall right at the moment they could clinch it. This is appointment viewing: the game's top pitcher NERD score of the day belongs to a Cy Young frontrunner who could clinch a division title while touching 100+ mph, against a Pittsburgh bullpen game that exists mostly to survive nine innings.

Misiorowski has been, in the words of one outlet, "the favorite to win the NL Cy Young Award this year", sporting a 1.95 ERA and a 2.24 FIP with 236 strikeouts, and opponents are hitting just .156 against him this season. His pNERD of 14.73 is comfortably above today's field (max 14.73, average 5.46) thanks to elite strikeout stuff (100.6 mph average velocity) and a tiny xFIP-. Across from him, Lake Bachar is functionally a bullpen-game placeholder — Pittsburgh has used a bullpen game in that rotation spot led off by reliever Lake Bachar (1-3, 3.52) the last three turns through the starting order — and his 3.84 pNERD reflects the mismatch. The Brewers' 9.93 tNERD (elite baserunning, bullpen, and a young, cheap roster) dwarfs Pittsburgh's 6.83, though the Pirates aren't dead yet in the wild-card race and still bring solid baserunning and bullpen marks of their own. With a 17.67 gNERD, this sits near the top of both today's slate and the historical distribution — worth clearing your schedule for, division-clinch drama included.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Chicago White Sox @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:40p

Summary

A legitimate ace on the mound and a playoff race hanging in the balance make this the best watch of the day. Gavin Williams has quietly turned into a Cy Young dark horse this year, not named an All-Star but the type of pitcher who "wouldn't be surprising whatsoever" to get Cy Young votes come November, and he passed 200 strikeouts on August 20th. His 12.71 pNERD is elite - a 67 xFIP-, mid-90s velocity, and a filthy strikeout rate all point to a pitcher who can miss bats and rack up value in a hurry. Newcomb is a serviceable complement with an 89-good xFIP- but nothing special, and his fringe stuff and lack of consistency mean this game leans heavily on Williams' shoulders. The stakes matter too: the AL Central rivals are jockeying for postseason positioning, with Cleveland fighting to hang onto its wild-card grip while Chicago sits atop the division. Both offenses carry youth and low payrolls that boost their tNERD marks, though Cleveland's below-average barrel rate is a real soft spot. At 16.73, this gNERD sits well above today's 11.03 average and near the historical 95th percentile - genuinely one of the better games on the board.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:40p

Summary

Skubal on the mound is reason enough to tune in—the reigning two-time AL Cy Young winner has been a revelation since arriving from Detroit, and this is a rematch of the beatdown he put on Cincinnati just last week. In that September 9 start, he worked into the eighth inning against these same Reds, allowing just two runs on four hits with five strikeouts across 7 1/3 innings. His pNERD of 11.91 is comfortably above today's slate average, driven by elite whiff and strike rates and a fastball that still sits at 96.8 mph. Across his run with LA, Skubal is 2-2 with a 2.93 ERA and 48 strikeouts over 43 innings, and his xFIP- suggests he's actually pitching even better than that shiny ERA implies.

Lodolo, by contrast, is the exact opposite story — a 2.03 pNERD reflecting a rough season where his last three starts have been even shakier at a 5.52 ERA, with command issues (38 walks) fueling the mismatch. The Reds counter with some thump — De La Cruz has been an absolute terror at the plate, crushing a 444-foot home run off Skubal on September 9 — but the Dodgers own a clear tNERD edge (8.02 to 4.75), buoyed by strong batting and bullpen numbers. At 13.35, this game's gNERD lands solidly above the historical median and near today's average, making it a reasonably watchable pick, mostly on the strength of watching an ace work.

Miami Marlins @ Arizona Diamondbacks, 6:40p

Summary

Not exactly a marquee pitching duel on paper, but the backstory carries this one: Corbin Burnes making just his second start back from Tommy John surgery, still on a strict pitch count, against a Marlins team clinging to fading wild-card hopes. Sandy Alcantara has been the workhorse of the National League — he leads the majors with 21 quality starts and 200 innings pitched, the first time he's hit that plateau since his 2022 Cy Young season — but he's been scuffling lately, allowing 11 earned runs over just 10.1 innings across his last two September starts. Burnes, meanwhile, looked sharp in his return, tossing three scoreless innings on 57 pitches against Kansas City, though his cutter velocity is still a tick down from last year. Since Burnes has no track record yet this season, his pNERD sits at zero, dragging the pitching score down despite Alcantara's plus fastball velocity carrying his end. The Marlins' tNERD (8.97) stands out thanks to strong baserunning, a young inexpensive roster, and some positive regression-to-come luck, while Arizona's solid defense keeps its offer respectable. Overall gNERD of 12.38 sits comfortably above the historical and today's averages — watchable, if only to see how far Burnes can stretch it.

Atlanta Braves @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Chicago's offense is legit right now, and this game carries real stakes with October seeding on the line, but both starters are walking a tightrope that could turn this into a slugfest rather than a pitchers' duel. The Cubs, boasting the best tNERD score in today's slate (10.53, driven by an elite batting-runs mark and standout fielding), host a Braves club that's cooled off, dropping five of its last ten and losing four straight to Philadelphia before salvaging one game against Tampa Bay. Reynaldo López is making just his second start back from a knee injury that sidelined him for weeks, and his return outing wasn't pretty — he just surrendered six runs across 4 2/3 innings during his return from a knee injury. David Peterson owns the better pNERD here (5.23 vs. López's 3.15), helped by strong luck-based regression upside, but his control has been shaky too — he's issued 59 walks in 131.1 innings, with three or more walks in three of his last four starts. With home field for October at stake and Pete Crow-Armstrong's 41 homers looming, expect fireworks more than finesse — this one's watchable for the stakes and the lineups, even if the pitching doesn't inspire much confidence, landing solidly above the historic gNERD median.

Detail

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Miami Marlins, 10:40a

Summary

A high-strikeout, high-drama series finale that ranks near the top of the day's watchability board, thanks to two hard-throwing arms who can't quite stay out of their own way. This one caps a weekend set in Miami with the Dodgers (90-58, riding an 8-2 stretch) looking to close out the Marlins (73-76, losers of seven of ten) in a dome that's been pitcher-friendly all year. Emmet Sheehan's 5.08 ERA undersells him — he's racked up 118 strikeouts in 101 innings and just struck out 10 over 5.2 innings in a 6-3 win over Cincinnati, and his pNERD (7.29) reflects a nasty swinging-strike rate and youthful upside. Eury Pérez, at just 23 with a mid-90s-plus fastball touching 98, has been electric but leaky lately — he's allowed five-plus runs while failing to reach the fifth inning in three straight outings, walking four against Washington and three against the Mets. Both bullpens are taxed after a bullpen-heavy Saturday, adding some late-inning intrigue. With a gNERD of 15.66 — comfortably above today's 11.35 average and near the historic 95th percentile — and Miami's tNERD boosted by youth, baserunning, and some positive luck, this game earns its spot near the top of the watch list even without a marquee team on paper.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

Paul Skenes still owns the game's watchability, even though his season line hasn't matched his Cy Young-caliber ceiling, and this Cubs-Pirates rubber match carries real playoff stakes for Chicago. This is the highest gNERD score on the board today (16.09 against a 7.44–16.09 range), driven mostly by an excellent Cubs team and a dominant arm. Skenes brings a 9.80 pNERD - elite by any measure, powered by plus velocity, a hefty swinging-strike rate, and youth on his side - though he's been homer prone. He's struggled in two starts versus the Cubs this season, going 0-2 with a 5.06 ERA, and is 2-4 with a 3.45 ERA in nine career appearances against Chicago, so there's a real revenge-game angle here. Clay Holmes (4.99 pNERD) is comparatively pedestrian but serviceable, and he's been Chicago's steadiest arm all September. The Cubs' 10.36 tNERD is elite - built on standout batting and fielding runs - while Pittsburgh's roster is dealing with injuries to Braxton Ashcraft, Mitch Keller, Endy Rodríguez, Kirby Yates, and now outfielder Esmerlyn Valdez. Add in Alex Bregman's two-run homer and near-cycle in Friday's 12-2 win, his 25th of the season, and you've got a marquee arm facing a hot lineup with something to prove on both sides.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

A dominant Dodgers ace against a fading Marlins club still makes for a solid watch, mostly thanks to Tyler Glasnow's clean stuff. Glasnow is 4-0 with a 3.12 ERA and 10.9 strikeouts per nine innings in his return from the injured list, and this is his fourth start since returning from the injured list—he's been especially sharp against Miami specifically, 2-0 with a 1.59 ERA in three career starts at loanDepot park. His pNERD of 8.83 is well above average, built on elite xFIP- and above-average velocity and whiff rates. Phillips, by contrast, is a league-average arm who started the season in the bullpen but since joining the rotation has a 4.23 ERA and 4.91 xERA in 17 starts—his 4.95 pNERD reflects that mediocrity, though his underlying stuff isn't bad. The Dodgers arrive at 90-57 and lead the National League West, while Miami has lost four in a row. Miami's tNERD (9.00) actually edges LA's (7.90), fueled by a young, cheap roster outperforming its underlying batted-ball data—positive regression could be coming. Combined 15.34 gNERD sits near the top of today's slate, and comfortably above the historical average, making this an easy recommend if you like watching a real ace work.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

This one's near the top of the board today, thanks largely to a Cubs offense and defense that's humming and a pitching mismatch that's more interesting than it looks on paper. Chicago's Shota Imanaga takes a full week of rest into this one and has flat-out owned Pittsburgh this year — he has dominated the Pirates twice this season with a combined 12 scoreless innings, 13 strikeouts, two walks, and just four hits. His whiff rate and contact-suppression numbers back it up, giving him a solid pNERD score even if his home-run rate has been a season-long headache. Opposite him: Wilber Dotel, who is making his first big-league start in place of injured All-Star Braxton Ashcraft, after pitching out of the bullpen all season — an unknown-stats zero on the pNERD ledger, essentially a bullpen game for Pittsburgh. The Cubs' tNERD is elite, powered by top-shelf batting and fielding runs, offset only by a shaky bullpen; Pittsburgh counters with strong baserunning but leaky defense. Combined, this gNERD checks in comfortably above the historical average and leads the day's slate — worth tuning in, especially to see if Dotel can hang with a rested Imanaga.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Miami Marlins, 4:10p

Summary

A near-average matchup on paper turns intriguing once you clock who's actually walking to the mound. The gNERD of 13.37 sits comfortably above the historic median (10.81) and today's average (10.68), driven almost entirely by the Marlins' surprisingly frisky tNERD of 9.11 — powered by strong baserunning, a young, cheap roster, and some positive regression coming their way after a bit of bad luck.

The pitching probables listed here mark Ryan Gusto's opponent as TBD, but the confirmed pitching matchup features Dodgers lefty Blake Snell and Marlins right-hander Ryan Gusto, a contrast between Snell's high-strikeout profile and Gusto's command-and-mix approach, and Snell's excellent form (an elite strikeout arm) should make this more watchable than the data-blank pNERD suggests. Gusto himself grades out fine (4.51 pNERD) thanks to strong strike-throwing, though he has shown enough vulnerability — nine home runs allowed in 72.1 innings — to invite concern.

The story on the field: the Dodgers enter at 89-57 and lead the National League West, having won seven straight and outscored opponents by 21 runs over their last 10, including a 14-1 rout of Cincinnati, while Miami has dropped three straight and gone 3-7 over its last ten, though the Marlins are not without weapons at home, where they own a 43-32 record. Worth tuning in if you like watching a hot team try to keep rolling against a scrappy, undermanned host.

Summary

Cleveland's Parker Messick against Minnesota's Taj Bradley is the kind of pitching matchup that makes a September game worth clearing your schedule for. Messick has quietly become one of the AL's best arms, an All-Star this year who struck out a career-high 12 batters over six innings in his last start, and he's been almost unfair lately, allowing one earned run or fewer in three of his last four starts. His 8.49 pNERD is well above today's average, built on strong xFIP-, a quick pace on the mound, and his youth. Bradley isn't far behind at 7.32, pairing plus velocity with a respectable strikeout rate, though he's allowing four earned runs or more in two of his last three starts — some rust to shake off. The gNERD of 12.90 sits comfortably above the historic median and today's average, driven almost entirely by pitching. Cleveland's tNERD (6.73) outpaces Minnesota's (3.26), reflecting Cleveland's younger roster, sturdier bullpen, and better baserunning, while the Twins limp in having lost five of the team's last seven games. Not a marquee offensive show, but a legitimate pitchers' duel with playoff stakes attached for Cleveland.

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

This is the top-rated game of the day, and it's not particularly close. A tightly-wound rubber match closes out the season series between the Cubs and Brewers, with Milwaukee riding a big NL Central cushion and eyeing a home sweep. Logan Henderson has quietly become one of the best young arms in baseball — sitting at 9-3 with a 2.48 ERA and a microscopic 0.79 WHIP across 83.1 innings — and his 8.73 pNERD backs that up, built on excellent strike-throwing and a stingy xFIP-. Gausman's been shakier of late but still owns a strong résumé; the two actually dueled six days ago, when these two starters combined for 14 innings and three earned runs in a 2-1 Cubs win. Both team offenses are lively — Chicago's power (led by a Pete Crow-Armstrong breakout) and Milwaukee's youthful, athletic lineup both grade out well in tNERD, with the Brewers boosted by strong fielding and bullpen work. Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

This one's a headliner: Jacob Misiorowski brings a 100-mph fastball and Cy Young-caliber numbers to a Brewers team chasing its fourth straight NL Central title, and the gNERD score of 20.24 backs that up as one of the best on the slate today (today's games top out at 20.24, well above the historic average of 10.81). Misiorowski's pNERD of 14.88 is elite even by exceptional standards—his xFIP- of 54 and a swinging-strike rate that dwarfs the league are legit, and his fastball has already rewritten the record books this year for pitch velocity. He's dominated Chicago this season, going 2-0 with a stingy ERA in three prior starts against the Cubs, though he did get roughed up for five runs in one of those outings—so he's not unhittable. On the other side, David Peterson (pNERD 5.31) has been homework since his midsummer arrival from the Mets, alternating flashes of grounder-heavy competence with second-half hard-contact trouble; he lasted only 3 2/3 innings last time he faced Milwaukee. Both lineups carry real thump—Chicago's fielding and batting runs are strong, and Milwaukee leads the NL in runs scored—giving this game high-scoring upside if Misiorowski falters, and a must-watch floor if he doesn't.

Washington Nationals @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

A tale of contrasting motivations: the Padres are scrapping for a wild-card spot while the Nationals are simply auditioning their kids, and that mismatch actually makes for a decent watch. San Diego is sitting 11 games back in the division but locked in a fight for the third NL wild-card spot, tied with Arizona, so every Petco Park frame carries weight, while Washington arrives having dropped its way to an eight-game road skid and is mostly playing spoiler. The tNERD gap favors San Diego thanks largely to an outstanding bullpen (+80.2 runs) against Washington's dreadful relief corps (-31.5), though the Nats counter with elite baserunning and a young, cheap roster that scores well on age and payroll. On the mound, Casey Mize has quietly turned into a useful arm — 5-9 with a 3.64 ERA, 1.12 WHIP and 100 strikeouts — giving him the pNERD edge, while rookie Riley Cornelio has no NERD data yet and is still finding his footing at 2-2 with a 5.96 ERA and 1.81 WHIP. Petco's pitcher-friendly dimensions could keep this crisp rather than a slugfest, with James Wood's .927 OPS the top thunder threat for Washington. A 13.76 gNERD lands comfortably above average for today's slate — worth a look if you like playoff stakes on one side and prospect-watching on the other.

Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

A tight NL Central race gives this one stakes, even if the arms on the mound are more workmanlike than dominant. Milwaukee holds a seven-game lead over Chicago, and with the Brewers looking to lock up the season series for tiebreaker purposes, this rematch of last week's series at Wrigley carries some late-season weight. Chicago won the most recent meeting 2-1, splitting a four-game series after Milwaukee had taken the middle two games by lopsided scores. Neither bullpen is fresh — Milwaukee's pen got overworked in a 12-8 loss in Cincinnati while Chicago's did the same in a 10-3 blowout in Miami, so neither unit arrives rested. Milwaukee is also without Brandon Woodruff and lost Quinn Priester for the season, forcing more bullpen reliance — but the Brewers' actual bullpen NERD component is strong, offsetting that. On the mound, Boyd and Gasser are both middling by NERD (3.92 and 4.74, roughly average for today's slate), though Gasser gets a bump from being unlucky this year. The real juice here is the offense and depth on both sides — this gNERD of 14.47 sits well above the historical average and near today's high end, making it one of the better watches on the board.

Cincinnati Reds @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

A rookie-adjacent ace with a wipeout slider takes the mound against baseball's best lineup, and the Reds' bullpen plan alone is worth the price of admission. This game rates 14.25 on the gNERD scale, comfortably above both the historic average (10.81) and today's slate average (11.60), and it's easy to see why once you look past the standings.

The headline is Chase Burns, whose 10.38 pNERD is well above the 95th percentile historically — he's been outstanding in 2026 with a 1.16 WHIP and a 28.9% strikeout rate that ranks among the best in the National League, fueled by upper-90s velocity and elite whiff rates. There's a wrinkle worth watching: a right elbow flexor strain briefly sidelined him this summer, and the Reds have been managing his workload carefully ever since, which explains why Terry Francona plans to piggyback Brandon Williamson behind Burns to keep his innings down. The Dodgers' response is a mystery-box TBD, reportedly journeyman/rookie fill-in Emmet Sheehan, whose stuff has been hittable in the minors.

Team-wise, the Dodgers (8.11 tNERD) bring a top-tier offense and bullpen, riding a four-game win streak, while the Reds (5.01 tNERD) are scuffling but oddly barrel the ball well. Not a must-watch pitching duel on paper, but Burns alone makes it worth tuning in early.

Nick Pivetta's return from a five-month elbow absence is the whole story here, and it's a genuinely fun one to tune into. The Padres are activating Pivetta off the 60-day IL for his first big-league start since he walked off the mound mid-rehab back in April, and last year he finished sixth in NL Cy Young voting behind a 2.87 ERA. His final tune-up was encouraging — "4⅓ scoreless innings and seven strikeouts on 64 pitches" — though the team has him on a restricted pitch count, so don't expect length. No sample exists yet for our pNERD model, hence his 0.00, but the small-sample peripherals (13.5 K/9, sub-1.15 WHIP) suggest real swing-and-miss stuff if the elbow holds. Jake Irvin, by contrast, is a well-quantified mess this year — his xFIP- and shaky command drag him to a middling 3.61 pNERD, salvaged only by tough luck. The Padres own the far better bullpen and broadcast ratings, pushing tNERD to a strong 9.48, and Washington's baserunning and pop give it a respectable 8.65 too. Miami's stealthy playoff push meets a Mets team basically running out the string with an intriguing arm, and the pitching matchup alone makes this worth a look. Eury Pérez brings a 7.27 pNERD built on a 98 mph fastball, elite swinging-strike rate, and a still-youthful frame at 23 — a career-low hard-hit rate and career-best ground-ball rate show he's evolving from thrower to pitcher even as his strikeout rate dips. Atlanta Braves @ Philadelphia Phillies, 10:05a

Summary

Jesús Luzardo is pitching like the best version of himself right now, and that alone makes this one worth clearing your schedule for. The Phillies lefty enters having been named NL Pitcher of the Month for August, and he's 5-0 with a 1.64 ERA across his last five outings, missing bats at an elite clip with 209 strikeouts on the season. His 10.51 pNERD is well above today's average of 5.91 and sits near the historic 95th percentile, backed by a filthy xFIP- of 70 and a fastball touching 96.5 mph — the run-prevention and swing-and-miss profile of a true ace. Grant Holmes is a serviceable if unspectacular counter, with a middling xFIP- and modest 3.57 pNERD, and reports note Holmes generates outs but invites baserunners at a higher rate than his counterpart.

The teams themselves are roughly average watchability-wise — both Atlanta and Philadelphia sit near league-median tNERD, though the Phillies get a bump from broadcast quality and Atlanta's bullpen has quietly been strong. Storyline-wise, Atlanta has already clinched the season series against Philadelphia, up 7-3 with four games left to play, and they've won three of the four meetings so far in this very series, giving this getaway-day finale some divisional pride on the line even with the standings largely settled.
